full_judgment: 2. Defendants are the appellants and the suit was for declaration of the plaintiff's title to the suit property, recovery of possession and for mandatory injunction. The case of the plaintiff, as set out in the plaint, is that the suit land, plots Nos. 1 and 2 of the Old Cantonment at Chittagong belonged to defendant No. 3, the- Government of Bangladesh in the Ministry of Defense. It was put to public-auction in which defendant No. 1, Ayaz Bahadur Khan, offered the highest bid whereupon it was leased out to him on 12.12.66 for a period of 30 years on a consideration of Rs. 93,000/ out of which an amount of Rs. 23,250/- was paid on that day. But as defendant No.1 could not pay the balance of Rs.69, 750/- he entered into an agreement with defendant No. 4 for sub-letting the land. According to the Agreement between them made on 23. 5. 69, defendant No. 4 paid to defendant No.1 an amount of Rs. 1, 10.000/- as rent in advance for the proposed sub-lease and also agreed to pay yearly rent to defendant No.1 at the rate of Rs.1, 600/- per month for the first 10 years, Rs. 1950/- per month for the second 10 years and Rs. 2,600/per month for the third 10 years. Further, defendant No. 4 agreed to construct a petrol pump, filling and service station on this land and to offer dealership for sale of petrol to defendant No. 1. In pursuance of this Agreement of sub-lease defendant No.1 delivered possession of the suit land to his sub-lessee, defendant No.4 who, in due course constructed a petrol pump station in which defendant No.1 started business of distributing petrol from 1970. But no lease-deed in pursuance of the auction held on 12 12.66 was yet executed and registered by defendant No. 3 on the ground that defendant No. 1, the lessee did not pay the rent from the date of auction, and when defendant No.2, the Military Estate Officer under defendant No.3 threatened to cancel the lease for non-payment of the arrears of rent defendant No.1 faced difficulties in procuring the necessary money to pay the rent. He approached the plaintiff to help him in the matter. Again, Defendant No.1 being a non-local was threatened with dire consequences by some persons if he did not leave the, suit property and other properties during the unsettled period following the war of liberation in 1971. In these difficulties the plaintiff came forward to the rescue of defendant No.1 who then entered into an agreement with him for sale of the suit land along with the petrol-pump agency thereon for a consideration of Tk. 83,000/-. The proposal was finalized on 3.3.72 in the F.I.D.C. Rest House at Chittagong and an amount of Tk. 20,000/- out of the total consideration of Tk. 83,000/- was paid by the plaintiff to defendant No.1 on that occasion against a plain paper receipt. Thereafter, on 4.6.72, the plaintiff and defendant No.1 executed a formal deed of agreement for sale in the office of the former at Dacca and on that occasion the plaintiff paid to defendant No.1 a further sum of Tk. 40,000/- against a plain paper receipt. The balance of Tk. 23,000/- of the total consideration was paid by the plaintiff to defendant No.1 in his office at Dacca on 8.7.72 against another plain paper receipt. Defendant No. 1, who had already sent his family to London, sold away his restaurant at Chittagong, the main source of his livelihood and made all preparation for leaving the country in order to join his family in London and in that connection he sought the plaintiff's help. The plaintiff, an advocate of the High Court and a member of the Bangladesh Jatiya Leagaue, promised all necessary help and contacted different persons both at home and abroad in order to get necessary travel documents for defendant No.1. On 9.7.72 defendant No.1 went to Calcutta and started to live there as he felt insecure of his life at Chittagong because of the abnormal situation which was continuing since the liberation. Defendant No.3, Government of Bangladesh, by an order dated the 22nd June, 1972 cancelled the defendant's lease on the ground of non-payment of rent whereupon the plaintiff rushed to Calcutta and informed the defendant (No. 1) of this development., Defendant No.1 then executed a General Power of Attorney dated 30.9.72 in favor of the plaintiff authorising him thereby to do all acts for protecting, and if necessary for selling his properties including the suit land. The plaintiff met the concerned authorities of the Directorate of Military Land and Cantonment at Dacca and got the order of cancellation of the lease revoked by paying the arrear rent on account of the lease. In pursuance of the Agreement for sale of the suit property defendant No.1 had already addressed a letter date 22.9.72 to the Director of Military Land and Cantonment advising him to "draw, execute and register" the necessary lease deed in favor of the plaintiff. Thereupon, defendant No. 2, the Military Estate Officer, after obtaining necessary sanction from the Government, executed and registered a Lease Deed on 20.4.73 in favor of the plaintiff as nominated by the auction purchaser, defendant No. 1. After execution of the Lease-Deed in his favor the plaintiff addressed a letter to defendant No. 4 intimating him of the change of ownership of the suit land and requesting him to transfer the petrol pump agency to him and also to pay rent of the suit land as sub-lessee under him. This change of ownership was also confirmed by defendant No.1 in a similar letter addressed to defendant No. 4. But defendant No.1 suddenly changed his mind and tried to avoid delivery of possession of the suit land since the value of the suit land increased in the meantime. Defendant No. 2, the Military Estate Officer also instructed defendant No.1 to undo the sale transaction whereupon defendant No.1, by his letter dated 16.6.73 informed the plaintiff that there was no contract for sale or no payment of consideration money whatever and that all the papers and documents, such as the Agreement for sale receipts for payment of consideration money were fabricated and forged by him (plaintiff). Defendant No. 4 also refused to recognise the plaintiff as the new owner in place of defendant No.1 and did not transfer the petrol pump agency. In these circumstances, the plaintiff filed this suit for declaration of title, recovery of possession and mandatory injunction.
